feedbackActionPlan.summary: Add an Other write-in option to the vault plate/ferrule color selector, charge a configurable custom color surcharge, flag the order for color availability review, and show clear line-item language in cart, checkout, admin, and confirmation summaries.
feedbackActionPlan.customerImpact: Customers who want a vault plate/ferrule color outside the standard palette can request it without abandoning the order or using ambiguous notes, while seeing the additional fee before checkout.
feedbackActionPlan.businessImpact: Captures paid custom color work, reduces manual quote follow-up, makes production review explicit, and prevents custom-color requests from being missed in free-form order notes.
feedbackActionPlan.confidence: The raw feedback directly asks for write-in colors with an additional fee, and related feedback clarifies that the customer-facing label should say vault plate/ferrule. This checkout appears to be a billiards simulation repository rather than the website codebase, so implementation surfaces are inferred from a typical product configurator, cart, checkout, order admin, and order email flow.

researchFindings.finding: The assigned raw feedback requests a section for other vault plate colors with an additional fee.
Related raw feedback says the option should be labeled vault plate/ferrule because customers may not understand vault plate alone.
The repository README describes a billiards diagram and physics simulation tool; no website configurator implementation surface was identified in this checkout.
Because custom colors can require material availability checks, the website should collect the request and surcharge up front while still marking the order for staff review before production.

implementationPlan.step: Find the existing vault plate color option definition in the product configurator source of the website, and rename the customer-facing group label to Vault plate/ferrule color if that terminology is not already used.
Add Other / custom color as the final option in the vault plate/ferrule color choices, visually separated from standard colors if the UI supports grouping.

When Other is selected, reveal a required text input labeled Requested vault plate/ferrule color with helper text such as Enter the color or material look you want; custom colors include an additional fee and are reviewed for availability.

Validate the write-in value on the client and server: trim whitespace, require a non-empty value only when Other is selected, set a reasonable length limit, reject markup, and preserve the exact customer wording in the order record.
Add a configurable custom vault plate/ferrule color surcharge in the pricing model rather than hard-coding the amount in UI text.

Update price calculation so selecting Other adds one surcharge line item exactly once, removes it when the customer returns to a standard color, and includes it in cart, checkout, tax/shipping calculations as applicable, payment authorization, and order totals.
Persist structured order data with separate fields for selected color option, custom color text, surcharge amount charged, and a boolean review flag such as requiresCustomColorReview.
Add an internal review workflow signal in admin order views and production exports: display Needs review: custom vault plate/ferrule color, the requested color text, and the fee already collected.

Update cart, checkout, order confirmation, customer email, and admin summary language to read Vault plate/ferrule color: Other - customer text, with a separate Custom vault plate/ferrule color fee: $X line item.

If staff may reject unavailable colors, define the operational path: contact customer with alternatives, keep the surcharge if a custom alternative is accepted, or refund/remove the surcharge if the customer chooses a standard color.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Vault plate/ferrule color offers standard choices plus an Other / custom color option.
Selecting Other reveals a required write-in field; selecting a standard color hides the field and clears or ignores custom text.
The custom color surcharge is configurable and appears as a distinct line item in cart, checkout, payment total, order confirmation, and admin order detail.
Order summaries use customer-readable language: Vault plate/ferrule color: Other - requested color, plus Custom vault plate/ferrule color fee: $X.
Orders with Other selected are flagged for staff review and expose the requested color and charged surcharge in the production/admin workflow.
Server-side validation prevents submitting Other without a requested color and prevents charging the surcharge for standard colors.
Changing between Other and standard colors updates totals deterministically without duplicate surcharge lines.

risks.risk: If the surcharge amount is hard-coded in multiple places, future price changes can create checkout and admin mismatches.
Customers may assume any color is guaranteed unless the UI says custom colors are reviewed for availability.
Free-form color text can be too vague for production unless staff review is required and visible.
If payment capture happens before review, unavailable color requests need a clear refund or substitution process.

openQuestions.question: What exact surcharge amount should be charged for Other vault plate/ferrule colors?
Which standard vault plate/ferrule colors should remain no-fee options?
Should the surcharge be refundable if staff cannot source the requested color?
Should custom color requests affect estimated production lead time shown to the customer?
